recreation_brief: 1. Create a white-background slide. 2. Add a small yellow circle at the extreme top-right with black text '33'. 3. On the left, build five white rectangles with thick red borders in a staggered grid: Threshold=0.0 (top-left), Threshold=0.6 (top-center), Threshold=0.1 (mid-left), Threshold=0.3 (lower-mid-left), Threshold=0.4 (bottom-left). 4. Inside each red box, place a bold red header 'Threshold=X.X', a small 2x2 table with 'Predicted as' over columns P/N and 'Actual' beside rows P/N, fill the four cells with the specified counts, and add the TPR/FPR formulas to the right of each table. 5. Color the Actual-P row numbers dark red and the Actual-N row numbers dark blue/black. 6. Add a blue-bordered white box in the center-bottom area with bold red text 'ROC Curve for Same Model - different thresholds'. 7. On the right, draw a blue-bordered white rectangle for the ROC plot. Add x-axis 'FPR' and y-axis 'TPR' with ticks 0.0–1.0, light gray gridlines, and a blue diagonal line from bottom-left to top-right. 8. Plot five red circles at approximate positions (0.0, high), (0.1, high), (0.3, high), (0.4, mid), (0.6, mid) and label them '0.0', '0.1', '0.3', '0.4', '0.6'. 9. Below the plot, write the fraction formulas TPR = TP/(TP+FN) and FPR = FP/(FP+TN). 10. Beneath the formulas, draw a 2x2 legend table with 'Predicted as' P/N headers and 'Actual' P/N row labels; fill cells with TP (green background), FN, FP, TN.
